# Incident Report — Traffic Analysis Exercise, 2024‑08‑15

## Evidence Reviewed
- `2024-08-15-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (18,189 frames, 04:09:43–04:42:26 UTC+4)
- No separate IDS/Suricata alert export was present in the evidence directory — only the pcap. All findings below are derived directly from packet content (DHCP, DNS, Kerberos, HTTP, and file carving via `tshark`).

## Victim Host
| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.8.15.133** (DHCP lease; host briefly declined an earlier offer of 10.8.15.132) |
| MAC address | **00:1c:bf:03:54:82** |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-H8ALZBV** (DHCP option 12 and NBNS `<00>`/`<20>` registrations; AD-joined as `WIN-JEGJIX7Q9RS.lafontainebleu.org`) |
| Windows domain | LAFONTAINEBLEU |
| Logged-in user | **plucero** (seen as Kerberos AS-REQ client principal `plucero` from 10.8.15.133 to the domain controller at 10.8.15.4) |

## Malware Family
**Internal project name: "knock" (v1.1.8)** — identified from an embedded PDB debug path in the payload DLL:
```
E:\work\ooooooops\181\knock_v1.1.8\knock\bin64\knock.pdb
```
This is a **behavioral/artifact-based identification, not signature-confirmed**. No IDS/AV alert file was provided with this evidence, and no internet-based hash or threat-intel lookup was performed (per instructions). The determination rests on: the embedded PDB string above, the module's minimal import set (ADVAPI32, KERNEL32, SHELL32, WS2_32, ole32 — consistent with a lightweight loader/backdoor stub), a mutex-check pattern (`CreateMutexW`/`OpenMutexW`), and its custom HTTP C2 protocol (`CMD=POLL`/`ACK=1` keep-alive and `CMD=ENCD`/`DATA=` encoded exfil/tasking, observed in plaintext inside HTTP bodies).

## Infection Chain (reconstructed from traffic)
1. **04:10:58** — Host requests `quote.checkfedexexp.com` (Cloudflare-fronted, 104.21.55.70 / 172.67.170.159), a fake FedEx/shipping-notice lure domain, via:
   `GET /managements?16553a25e45250a41fd5&endeds=MIGpq&JStx=59bf050d37df88a9-ade43358-eaa1220b-0571422b-0f33e6aa150e86bafd0ed4&Ld=9d7502d88d752a27b1d00587309184b5a215`
   Response body is a ZIP archive containing **`Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js`** (6.9 MB, heavily padded with unrelated benign text — a size-inflation/AV-evasion technique — SHA256 `dab98819d1d7677a60f5d06be210d45b74ae5fd8cf0c24ec1b3766e25ce6dc2c`).
2. **04:11:59** — Host uses Microsoft **BITS** (`Microsoft BITS/7.8` UA) to pull a second-stage PE32+ DLL directly from the raw C2 IP:
   `GET http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4`
   This file is the **"knock" loader DLL** (SHA256 `b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6`).
3. **04:13:00 onward** — Host begins sustained HTTP beaconing to the same C2 IP (**342 distinct TCP sessions** over the following ~29 minutes, through the end of the capture at 04:42:26), each carrying a large base64-like encoded blob in the `Cookie` header, with `User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)`. Every observed beacon response was **HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request**, indicating the C2 endpoint was non-responsive/dead for the remainder of the capture window.

Note: a `GET /assets/Owner/arm/ProcessMAU.txt` to `acroipm2.adobe.com` (a legitimate Adobe domain) and Windows/Edge/BITS traffic to `msedge.b.tlu.dl.delivery.mp.microsoft.com` were also observed but are consistent with normal Adobe/Windows background activity, not part of the malicious chain.

## Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control**
- `72.5.43.29:80` (HTTP, `Host: 72.5.43.29`) — 342 beacon sessions, `CMD=POLL`/`ACK=1` and `CMD=ENCD`/`DATA=` protocol observed in cleartext HTTP bodies.

**Malicious domains**
- `quote.checkfedexexp.com`
- `business.checkfedexexp.com`
- Resolved IPs: `104.21.55.70`, `172.67.170.159` (Cloudflare)

**Malicious URLs**
- `http://quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?16553a25e45250a41fd5&endeds=MIGpq&JStx=59bf050d37df88a9-ade43358-eaa1220b-0571422b-0f33e6aa150e86bafd0ed4&Ld=9d7502d88d752a27b1d00587309184b5a215`
- `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4`

**Transferred files**
| File | SHA256 | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js` | `dab98819d1d7677a60f5d06be210d45b74ae5fd8cf0c24ec1b3766e25ce6dc2c` | Delivered inside ZIP from `quote.checkfedexexp.com`; JS dropper/downloader, junk-padded to 6.9 MB |
| `0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` (staging name on C2) | `b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6` | PE32+ DLL, x86-64; PDB path `E:\work\ooooooops\181\knock_v1.1.8\knock\bin64\knock.pdb`; delivered via BITS |

## Summary
DESKTOP-H8ALZBV (10.8.15.133, MAC 00:1c:bf:03:54:82), logged in as domain user `plucero` (LAFONTAINEBLEU\plucero), was compromised via a fake-FedEx-invoice phishing/download page at `quote.checkfedexexp.com`. This delivered a padded JavaScript dropper, which used BITS to fetch a loader DLL (internal build name "knock" v1.1.8) from `72.5.43.29`. The loader then beaconed to `72.5.43.29:80` for roughly 29 minutes using a custom `CMD=POLL/CMD=ENCD` HTTP protocol; the C2 server answered every beacon with HTTP 400, suggesting it was inactive/sinkholed for the remainder of the capture.
